text:
Minnesota's third straight win came with a goalie who made the Sharks pay for every mistake. Jesper Wallstedt, drafted 20th overall by the Wild in 2021 and the top-ranked international goalie in his class, stopped 23 of 24 shots and saved about one goal more than the chances against him should have allowed. That kept the score level through a first period in which San Jose created the single best look of the night, a 28% chance from Ivar Stenberg that went wide.

The ending was lopsided, and our numbers say it was earned. Minnesota deserved to win 75% of the time, meaning that share of simulated replays of every shot go the Wild's way. The Wild finished at 3.71 expected goals (a measure of chance quality) to San Jose's 2.13, and took the third period 1.46 to 0.36. Even strength was close, 1.53 for SJS and 1.47 for MIN, so the gap came from the power play: Minnesota scored on two of five chances, with Kirill Kaprizov and Quinn Hughes assisting on the second one by Maxim Shabanov, while the Sharks went 0 for 3. Macklin Celebrini's tip-in tied it at 1-1 in the second, but Shabanov answered just over two minutes later. Hughes made it 3-1 early in the third, and Zach Bogosian's slap shot on a 2% chance sealed it.

Kaprizov, picked 135th in 2015, finished with a goal and three assists, and Hughes added a goal and two assists in 31 minutes. For San Jose, the loss extends a winless stretch to four games (0-4-0). Minnesota, meanwhile, carries a three-game winning streak into its next one.
